title: Berkshire 2023 AGM morning: float, buybacks, Apple, Japan, and succession
summary: Buffett opens the 2023 Berkshire meeting explaining operating earnings, retained earnings, and insurance float as a liability that works like free equity. He then covers Geico and reinsurance, Apple, the Japanese trading houses, buybacks, succession, and why he is still optimistic about America.

principles.text: Judge Berkshire by operating earnings; stock prices swing capriciously, but you should expect capital gains over time.
principles.quote: we expect to make capital gains over time why would we own the stocks otherwise uh doesn't always work out but overall it works out pretty well over time but in any day any quarter any year even occasionally over a five-year period uh the stock prices move around capriciously

principles.text: Float is a liability that finances assets like equity but costs nothing, and cannot vanish quickly; most insurers don't think of it this way.
principles.quote: float is another item that shows a it's a liability but hasn't cost us anything and it it can't disappear in a hurry and it finances the asset side in the same way as stockholders equity and nobody else thinks of it much that way

principles.text: Retain earnings and compound; Berkshire's size came from keeping the money, and the one dividend paid was a mistake.
principles.quote: the reason we've gotten to where we are is because we we kept the money we did pay a dividend in nineteen sixty seven ten cents to share it was a terrible mistake

principles.text: Buy back stock only when it's below intrinsic value and after funding the business; it's simple, not complicated.
principles.quote: if you've got ample capital and you don't see that you're going to use it all and your stock is attractive and it enhances the intrinsic value for the remaining shareholders it's an old-brainer and if it's if it's above the price of intrinsic value it's a no-brainer

principles.text: Concentration beats broad diversification when you know where your competence ends; an Apple stake is a business like any other.
principles.quote: if you know the edge of your own ability pretty well you should ignore most of the Notions of our experts about what I call diversification of portfolios

principles.text: Opportunities come from other people doing dumb things and from a short-term-focused world; don't play games you needn't play.
principles.quote: what gives you opportunities is other people doing dumb things
